rules.claim: Whether a proposed window [proposed_start, proposed_end] is offerable given existing busy intervals on the same date. The deciding expression is the temporal overlap test between the proposed interval and each busy interval.

decision_semantics.predicate: window is offerable iff FOR ALL busy_intervals: NOT(proposed_start < busy.end AND proposed_end > busy.start) — exact inequality (strict vs. inclusive at the shared boundary) is unresolved
decision_semantics.boundary_behavior: UNRESOLVED: Whether a busy interval ending at 09:00 blocks a slot starting at 09:00 (i.e., whether the test uses < vs <= at the boundary) could not be established from production code

rules.claim: Which existing bookings produce busy intervals that block the proposed window: status filter (exclude cancelled?), host scoping (same user? same team?), and date-range scoping.

decision_semantics.predicate: busy set = { b ∈ bookings : b.userId ∈ hosts(event_type) AND b.status ∉ {cancelled} AND b overlaps booking_date } — exact status exclusion list and host resolution are unresolved
decision_semantics.boundary_behavior: UNRESOLVED: Whether 'ACCEPTED' vs 'PENDING' bookings both block slots, and whether team-member bookings all contribute, is not established

rules.claim: A proposed window must lie within the schedule's working hours for that day-of-week and (potentially) align to the slot-interval grid. Windows outside the schedule are unofferable regardless of busy times.

decision_semantics.predicate: window is schedule-valid iff proposed_start >= schedule.startTime(day) AND proposed_end <= schedule.endTime(day) AND (proposed_start - schedule.startTime) % interval == 0 — the modulo/grid constraint is unresolved
decision_semantics.boundary_behavior: UNRESOLVED: Whether a window ending exactly at schedule.endTime is valid (inclusive boundary) and whether off-grid starts are rejected are not established
